key_insight: Strong diagnostic performance did not ensure reliable downstream cancer care, with dominant failures shifting from staging errors to omissions in work-up and follow-up.
engineering_relevance: Clinical AI systems need phase-aware evaluation and safeguards rather than relying on diagnostic benchmarks or increasingly detailed prompts alone.
method: Introduced NPC-RubricBench for six sequential phases of nasopharyngeal carcinoma care.
Scored responses against patient-specific atomic criteria using only evidence available at decision time.
Evaluated 30 general-purpose and medical LLMs and varied query granularity.
evidence_signal: The benchmark covers 405 patients from two cancer centers, 941 patient-phase units, and 17,688 criteria; explicit decision errors dominated staging at 48.2%, while omissions dominated work-up and follow-up at 33.4% and 30.4%, respectively.
watch_item: Checklist-like prompts improved Decision Quality but reduced Evidence Faithfulness and Safety Adherence, requiring evaluation of these trade-offs before deployment.
paper_title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
